newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean won ends down ahead of import settlements.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean won ends down ahead of import settlements.

text.p: The won closed lower against the dollar on Thursday on the strength of dollar build-ups ahead of importer settlements due on Friday and Monday, brokers said.
"Dollar demand was steady in anticipation of importer deals despite early profit taking," said Park Se-gull of the Korea Exchange Bank.
The won closed at 822.80 after opening at 822.50. It ranged from 821.60 to 823.00.
Brokers said dollar buying was limited by fears of the central bank's dollar sales. "Intervention is possible at any levels between 820 and 825," said a local bank dealer.
The won's mid-rate is expected to be pegged at 822.30 on Friday, compared with 821.10 on Thursday.
Dealers said widening trading deficit was a major reason for rising dollar demand.
"But dollars are expected to flow in when the foreign stock ownership limit is expanded in October, limiting the dollar's rise," said a dealer with a foreign bank.
He predicted trading would range from 821.00 to 823.50 on Friday.
